title: Dome of the Rock completed
description: Caliph Abd al-Malik finished the domed shrine over the rock, the oldest surviving large Islamic monument and the city's most famous silhouette.

title: Ottoman rule begins
description: After defeating the Mamluks, Sultan Selim I took Jerusalem and the whole of Syria and Palestine into the Ottoman Empire, which ruled for four hundred years.

title: Arab revolt in Palestine
description: Peasants and townsmen rose against Egyptian conscription, holding Jerusalem and Nablus for weeks before Ibrahim Pasha crushed the rising at Hebron.

title: Nabi Musa riots
description: Riots during the Nabi Musa festival left dead and wounded on both sides, the first large violence between Arabs and Jews under British rule.

title: Hebron massacre
description: Rioters killed sixty-seven of Hebron's Jews during a week of countrywide disturbances, ending the city's ancient Jewish community.

title: Arab Revolt begins
description: Arab committees declared a general strike against British rule and Jewish immigration, opening a three-year revolt put down at great cost.

title: Peel Commission report
description: The royal commission first proposed dividing Palestine into two states with population transfers, rejected by the Arab leadership.

title: White Paper
description: Parliament approved the White Paper limiting Jewish immigration and land purchase and promising an Arab-majority state within ten years, on the eve of the world war.

title: Deir Yassin massacre
description: Irgun and Lehi fighters killed over a hundred villagers in an attack whose echoes drove Palestinian flight and the memory of the Nakba.

title: All-Palestine Government
description: The Arab League sponsored a Palestinian government in Egyptian-held Gaza, sidelined within months and abolished in 1959.

title: Fatah founded
description: Yasser Arafat and fellow exiles formed the underground movement that went on to lead the Palestinian national struggle.

title: PLO founded
description: The first Palestine National Council, meeting at the Ambassador Hotel, established the Palestine Liberation Organization, later recognised as representing the Palestinian people.

title: Arab League backs the PLO
description: The Rabat summit named the PLO the sole legitimate representative of the Palestinian people, and Arafat addressed the UN weeks later.

title: Declaration of independence
description: The Palestine National Council meeting in exile proclaimed the State of Palestine, recognised within months by scores of states.

title: Palestinian Authority formed
description: Under the Cairo agreement, Palestinian self-rule began in Gaza and Jericho, and Arafat returned from exile in July.

title: First elections
description: Palestinians elected Arafat president and a legislative council in the first general vote under self-rule.

title: Siege of the Church of the Nativity
description: Israeli forces besieged Palestinian fighters and others in the Bethlehem basilica for five weeks until a deal sent the wanted men into exile.

title: Arafat dies
description: Yasser Arafat died in a hospital near Paris after two years confined to his Ramallah headquarters, where he was buried.

title: Mahmoud Abbas elected president
description: Abbas won the presidential election to succeed Arafat, on a platform of negotiation.

title: Hamas wins the elections
description: Hamas defeated Fatah in legislative elections, a result that split Palestinian politics and brought international sanctions on the new government.

title: Hamas takes over Gaza
description: After months of factional fighting Hamas seized control of the Gaza Strip, leaving the West Bank and Gaza under rival administrations.

title: Gaza War
description: Israel's three-week air and ground campaign, launched to stop rocket fire, killed over a thousand Palestinians and left much of Gaza in ruins.

title: Palestine joins UNESCO
description: UNESCO admitted Palestine as a member, the first UN agency to do so, prompting the United States to cut its funding.

title: UN observer state
description: The General Assembly voted 138 to 9 to make Palestine a non-member observer state, opening the door to UN agencies and courts.

title: Gaza War
description: Seven weeks of war killed more than two thousand in Gaza, the deadliest of the rounds of fighting around the strip.

title: Great March of Return
description: Weeks of mass demonstrations at the Gaza fence for the right of return ended with Israeli fire killing hundreds of protesters.
